comment: Shared sha256-hex vectors, read by both suites, so a hash implementation that hashes the wrong bytes (a timestamp-prefixed wire payload, or a decoded string re-encoded differently) cannot pass in one language while failing in the other. Every input is plain bytes, exactly what a clipboard holds -- never the [ts][text] wire payload. sha256 is lowercase hex, no separators: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()'s native format, which Swift's sha256Hex must match byte for byte. Each value was verified independently via `python3 -c "import hashlib; print(hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest())"` before being committed here -- this file is not derived from either implementation under test.
